To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
associative memory and visual memory are negatively correlated with each other, and that associative memory and the spatial user interface are positively correlated with each other.

associative memory is strongly correlated with the ability to perform a task with a spatial user interface that is designed to facilitate associative retrieval; visual memory, on the other hand, is negatively correlated with the ability of users to perform the same task.

associative memory is positively correlated with the use of a visual user interface for information retrieval, and visual memory is negatively correlated with the use information visualisation techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between the cognitive abilities of users in information retrieval, and the design of user interfaces.
the design of a spatial user-interface for information retrieval.
the design of user interfaces for information retrieval tasks, and the role of cognitive abilities of users in the performance of these tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a spatial user interface is not a universal design solution for all types of retrieval tasks.
associative memory is important to users when performing information retrieval tasks with a spatial user interface.
the spatial user interface is not the best solution for all users.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

users with stronger associative memory tend to be better at finding relevant items in an information space, while users with stronger visual memory tend to be less effective in finding the relevant items.
users who have better associative and visual memory are likely to benefit from using a spatial user interface for information retrieval.
the design of a spatial user interfaces should be informed by the users’ memory abilities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a visual interface may be beneficial for users with a strong associative memory, and that a user's ability to visualise information is not necessarily correlated with his ability to use a visual user interface.
the design of a spatial user-interface for information retrieval tasks should take into consideration the users' memory abilities.
the design of user interfaces should take into consideration the memory abilities of users.
